notes: This is a state overview. Kentucky has 10 local workforce areas. In-school youth must be low-income and meet a listed barrier. Out-of-school youth must meet a listed barrier. Ask the youth career planner for your area about your case.
name: WIOA Youth Program
org: Kentucky Career Center, Department of Workforce Investment
what_you_do: Get help with school, job skills and career plans. Services can include paid or unpaid work, summer jobs, internships, job shadowing, tutoring and mentoring. Kentucky has 10 local workforce areas.
who_can_apply: In-school youth ages 14 to 21 who are low-income and have at least one listed barrier. A barrier can be being behind in basic skills or having a disability. Out-of-school youth are ages 16 to 24 and need at least one listed barrier, such as having dropped out of school.
pay_detail: Work experience can be paid or unpaid. Pay is not stated on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page
deadline_text: Programs run all year. No deadline is listed.
how_to_apply: Contact the youth career planner for your area. A map on the program page shows them. You can also contact any Kentucky Career Center office.
